objectClass.notes: Direct visual inspection shows one low padded moss-green mat with a broad rounded-rectangle plan, a darker wrapped perimeter, an inset continuous seam, and evenly segmented stitches. The unseen underside is inferred only as a thin non-slip support required for stable placement; no manufacturing-grade construction is claimed.

reasoning: The outer silhouette is geometrically simple, but the reference identity depends on a multi-part perimeter profile rather than a flat rounded box.
The evenly spaced stitch dashes form one dense curve-following repetition system around four sides and four large-radius corners.
Close-up insets expose distinct macro mottling, meso woven strands, and micro fiber/roughness breakup on both the field and binding.
The hidden underside and exact thickness are not visible, so those dimensions stay conservative and are reviewed through placement and contact-shadow behavior rather than claimed as reference fact.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate depth is sufficient for the simple massing, but strict fidelity requires explicit binding, seam and stitch systems plus independent three-frequency material response, a stable contact layer, and a rounded hit boundary.

detailInventory.note: Nine reference-observed or explicitly inferred implementation details are mapped to concrete localFeatures/localOverrides. Absolute underside thickness remains an inference, not a measured fact.

details.description: The outer plan uses four broad quarter-circle corners rather than a thin edge-radius clamp; corner radius is about 9 percent of mat depth.
details.scale: macro; radius approximately 0.55 world units for the preserved 6.25-unit depth

details.description: The central field is low and padded with a restrained convex crown, remaining nearly planar enough for desk use.
details.scale: meso; crown under 0.015 mat units above the edge datum

details.description: A darker continuous wrapped binding creates a rounded raised perimeter with a softly bulged cross-section.
details.scale: meso; approximately 0.055 mat units wide and 0.025 high
details.affects: perimeter profile, silhouette thickness, and edge highlight

details.description: A narrow recessed line separates the woven field from the wrapped binding around the complete inset perimeter.
details.scale: micro; groove width approximately 0.008 mat units
details.affects: edge construction line and cavity occlusion

details.description: Short moss thread dashes repeat at even spacing along all four sides and turn continuously through each corner.
details.scale: micro; dash length approximately 0.018 mat units with 0.028 spacing
details.affects: curve-following repeated geometry and thread-color contrast

details.description: Fine interlaced fibers form a dense directional crosshatch that remains visible in both the full view and close-up.
details.scale: micro; high-frequency weave repeated about 80 times per mat unit
details.affects: independent normal, roughness, and albedo channels

details.description: Broad low-contrast olive tonal variation prevents the field from reading as a uniform flat color without suggesting dirt.
details.scale: macro and meso; irregular variation over 0.12 to 0.45 mat units

details.description: The wrapped edge shows fine curved and longitudinal fiber marks following the perimeter instead of planar UV stretching.
details.scale: micro; fiber width below 0.003 mat units
details.affects: binding tangent-space normal and roughness direction

details.description: The outer crest of the rounded binding carries a restrained smoother highlight, strongest in the low grazing close-up.
details.scale: micro local mask over the outer 20 percent of binding width

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: At the reference three-quarter camera the preserved 8.7 by 6.25 world-unit footprint reads as a broad moss-green desk pad with large plan-view corner radii, never as a thin-radius rounded box.
The field, rolled binding, inset seam, and segmented perimeter stitches remain distinct from full-object distance and in a grazing edge close-up.
The field and binding each retain independently generated albedo, roughness, normal/height, and AO responses with macro, meso, and micro frequency bands.

The model rests without visible floating or wood intersection, uses one conservative rounded-rectangle collider/hit boundary, and does not alter the application's approved desk-mat interaction bounds.

featureGroups.name: Broad rounded plan silhouette and low profile
qualityCriteria: The approved 8.7 by 6.25 world-unit footprint and z=0.2 center stay unchanged; all four plan corners use a radius near 0.55 world units.
Side profile remains low and subtly padded; neither field nor binding balloons into a cushion.
failureModes: corner radius collapses because it is clamped by the thin vertical dimension
mat reads as a sharp slab, a pill, or a thick cushion

featureGroups.name: Layered field, binding, seam, and support structure
qualityCriteria: The central field, rolled binding, inset seam channel, repeated stitches, and thin non-slip underside have separate geometry/material ownership.
All layers share one root and a common rounded footprint so their boundaries stay registered.
failureModes: binding is painted onto the top surface instead of forming the reference edge profile
layers z-fight, separate, or produce an unintended gap at the corners

featureGroups.name: Inset segmented perimeter stitch system
qualityCriteria: Stitches are short raised thread segments instanced at even arc-length spacing around the complete inset rounded rectangle.
Corner orientation follows the path tangent with no bunching, straight-line shortcut, or missing quadrant.
failureModes: stitching is represented as one continuous painted outline
stitch spacing or tangent direction breaks visibly at the four corners
stitches float above the field or sink below the seam channel

featureGroups.name: Three-frequency woven field and wrapped binding response
qualityCriteria: Field and binding define independent albedo, roughness, normal/height, and AO maps; no channel aliases albedo.
Macro olive mottling, meso yarn variation, and micro crosshatch/fiber normal detail remain distinct under neutral and grazing light.
The binding crest has a localized smoother wear highlight while the inset seam and stitch contacts carry coherent AO.
failureModes: field reads as flat plastic or noisy stone rather than woven cloth
binding uses the field's planar texture and stretches around corners
normal detail is baked into albedo or disappears when relit

featureGroups.name: Grounded reference look-development and hit boundary
qualityCriteria: Reference-derived moss/olive palette and tactile response are verified in neutral, grazing, top, and reference-matched views.
One warm directional key plus restrained fill/environment preserves edge relief without flattening the mat.
The underside contact shadow anchors the model without a visible gap or intersection, and the rounded collider matches the outer footprint.
failureModes: the mat floats above or clips into the wooden desktop
lighting is evenly ambient and loses seam, stitch, and edge relief
hit boundary is a sharp rectangle or extends beyond the visible rounded footprint

visualDeltaChecks: preserved 8.7 by 6.25 footprint, 0.55 corner-radius, and low side-profile delta
field-to-binding width, height, and registration delta
inset seam path and stitch arc-length distribution delta
woven field and wrapped-edge macro/meso/micro response delta
localized binding crest highlight and contact AO delta
rounded collider-to-visible-footprint and desktop contact delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.

authoringInstruction: Assessment completed from direct inspection. Generate the sculpt spec with the skill script, preserve every mapped detail id, and validate both normal and strict-quality gates before implementation.
